covers: US open and global markets to 17:15 SAST Tuesday 3 November 2026, building on the 15:15 midday update
headline: Oil reverses: Brent drops 3.3% to $101 after Trump says US aid to Israel ends this year; Wall Street opens mixed as Apple and Palantir slide; US job openings beat at 7.5 million
summary: Oil turned lower during the afternoon: Brent was down 3.3% at $101.32 a barrel and WTI down 2.2% at $94.30 at 15:50 SAST, after President Trump said US payments to Israel would stop by the end of this year (Reuters via Euronext, 3 Nov). In New York the S&P 500 opened 0.10% higher at 7,549.17 and the Nasdaq 0.39% higher at 25,263.01, while the Dow fell 0.40% to 51,777.23 (Reuters via MarketScreener, 3 Nov); before the open Apple was down about 4%, Palantir about 6% and Shopify about 16% after results (StockTitan, 3 Nov), and US job openings for September came in at 7.5 million against about 7.13 million expected (BLS; Schwab, 3 Nov). In South Africa the rand was last seen near R16.62/$ ahead of Wednesday's local elections, when the JSE is closed, and new fuel prices take effect at 00:01 Wednesday with diesel R1.10–R1.20 a litre cheaper and petrol 1c cheaper (CNBC Africa/Reuters; Stuff, 3 Nov).

items.title: Oil reverses lower: Brent −3.3% to $101.32 after Trump says US aid to Israel ends this year
items.summary: Brent was down $3.45 (3.3%) at $101.32 a barrel at 13:50 GMT (15:50 SAST) and WTI down $2.16 (2.2%) at $94.30, giving back the morning's gains after the reported US strike on Qeshm Island. Trump told Fox & Friends that 'by the end of this year we won't be paying Israel' the $4 billion a year agreed earlier. Lower oil is a help for the rand and SA fuel prices, and a headwind for Sasol.

items.title: US job openings 7.5 million in September, above the ~7.13 million expected; quits rise to 3.4 million
items.summary: The Bureau of Labor Statistics said openings were 'little changed at 7.5 million', hires 5.4 million (3.4% rate) and quits rose to 3.4 million (released 17:00 SAST, 3 Nov). Schwab's preview had expected about 7.13 million openings and 3.05 million quits. A firmer labour market lowers the odds of quick Fed cuts; the October jobs report follows on Friday.
items.source: US Bureau of Labor Statistics, 3 Nov 2026; Charles Schwab, 3 Nov 2026

items.title: Australia's central bank raises rates to 4.85%, the highest since 2008, in a split 6–3 vote
items.summary: The Reserve Bank of Australia raised its cash rate by 0.25 percentage points to 4.85% from 4.60% at 05:30 SAST on Tuesday, its fifth increase this year and the highest level since November 2008; six board members voted to raise and three to hold (Domain; investingLive, 3 Nov). The bank said inflation will stay above target for longer than forecast, partly because of higher global fuel prices linked to the Middle East conflict, and does not expect it back in its 2–3% band until late 2027 (Domain, 3 Nov). Governor Michele Bullock gave no guidance on the next move, and the Australian dollar eased after the widely expected decision (investingLive, 3 Nov). It is another sign that oil-driven inflation is keeping central banks cautious, which matters for the SARB's next steps and for the rand.

items.title: Wall Street opens mixed on election day: S&P +0.10%, Nasdaq +0.39%, Dow −0.40%
items.summary: At 09:35 ET (16:35 SAST) the S&P 500 was up 7.77 points at 7,549.17, the Nasdaq Composite up 98.65 at 25,263.01 and the Dow down 206.75 at 51,777.23, as falling oil and the midterm vote set the tone. Chip stocks supported the Nasdaq after Monday's 1.1% drop.

items.title: Shopify down about 16% before the open after results; Apple −4%, Palantir −6%
items.summary: At 09:00 ET Shopify was down 15.82%, Apple 4.09% (about $202 billion of market value) and Palantir 6.22% (about $29 billion) versus Monday's close; AMD was more than 3% higher ahead of its results tonight.

items.title: Nasdaq-100 enters its third correction of the year on AI spending worries
items.summary: The Nasdaq-100 fell 1.39% on Monday 2 November to close at 27,989, about 10.4% below its record high of 6 October (near 31,400), putting it in a technical correction (a fall of 10% or more) for the third time in 2026. Worries about the returns on heavy AI spending after the big-tech results are the main driver (XTB, 3 Nov; Bloomberg, 2 Nov).

items.title: November fuel prices: diesel down R1.10–R1.20 a litre, petrol down only 1c from Wednesday
items.summary: From 00:01 on Wednesday 4 November, 93 and 95 petrol fall 1c a litre, diesel 0.05% falls R1.10 and diesel 0.005% R1.20, while illuminating paraffin (wholesale) rises R2.75 a litre and LPGas R1.83/kg, per the Department of Mineral and Petroleum Resources. The general fuel levy cut (R1.50/l petrol, R3/l diesel) is partly offset by a new slate levy of 135.84c/l. Cheaper diesel helps transport, farming and mining costs (Stuff, 3 Nov).

items.title: US letter gives 60 days' notice: SA's AGOA status to end on 1 January 2027
items.summary: BusinessTech reports that President Trump wrote to President Ramaphosa giving 60 days' notice that South Africa's AGOA trade beneficiary status will end on 1 January 2027, citing slow progress on corruption and trade barriers, and foreign policy concerns. Exporters of vehicles, citrus and other farm goods are the most exposed. On Monday the rand gained about 0.4% to R16.64/$ and traded at R16.62/$ on Tuesday morning; the Top-40 rose about 1% and the 2035 bond yield fell 2.5 basis points to 8.565%. NAAMSA new vehicle sales rose 10.4% year on year in October.

items.title: Rand steady near R16.62 on Tuesday; 2035 bond yield up 1.5bp to 8.51%
items.summary: The rand traded at R16.62/$ at 08:30 SAST, little changed from Monday's close, as investors weigh the US plan to suspend SA and Rwanda from AGOA from 1 January 2027; the 2035 government bond yield rose 1.5 basis points to 8.51% (CNBC Africa/Reuters, 3 Nov). SA holds local government elections on Wednesday, a public holiday, so the JSE is closed tomorrow.

items.title: JSE gold and PGM miners bounce 3–6% on Monday; Sasol falls 5.6% with oil
items.summary: On Monday 2 November Gold Fields rose 5.9% to R585.50, Implats 4.5% to R171.20, Harmony 4.1% to R255.70, AngloGold Ashanti 3.9% to R1,392 and Sibanye-Stillwater 3.3% to R36.96, recovering part of Friday's 5.6%–6.4% falls, while Sasol fell 5.6% to R273.20 as oil slumped (LRC Stock Scanner, 2 Nov 2026).

items.title: Brent $101.32 (−3.3%), WTI $94.30 (−2.2%) by mid-afternoon; morning high was about $106.60
items.summary: Brent was at $106.60 (+1.75%) at 06:42 ET before reversing to $101.32 (−3.3%) at 13:50 GMT; WTI was $94.30 (−2.2%). The US 10-year Treasury yield edged up to about 4.91%.
items.source: Reuters via Euronext, 3 Nov 2026; StockTitan, 3 Nov 2026

items.title: Gold slips about 1% to near $3,907 as the US votes
items.summary: Spot gold fell 1% to $3,906.71 an ounce during Tuesday trading (TokenPost, 3 Nov), after easing 0.5% to $3,926 earlier (Reuters, 3 Nov). Friday's one-year low was about $3,870.

items.title: AMD (LRC Stock Scanner: SELL, target $402.73) reports after the US close tonight
items.summary: AMD was more than 3% higher before the open ahead of third-quarter results due after 23:00 SAST (StockTitan, 3 Nov). The scanner's SELL rating and $402.73 target are unchanged; the results will be reviewed tomorrow morning.
items.source: StockTitan, 3 Nov 2026; LRC Stock Scanner, 3 Nov 2026

items.title: Lumentum closes 18.6% lower and Marvell 12.7% lower after their $115 billion all-stock deal
items.summary: Lumentum fell 18.59% to $684.40 and Marvell 12.72% to $171.41 on Monday (StockTitan, 2 Nov) after Marvell agreed to buy Lumentum for 4.5 Marvell shares per Lumentum share (Marvell press release, 2 Nov). Because the price is fixed in Marvell shares, Marvell's fall cuts the deal's value to Lumentum holders. LRC Stock Scanner (2 Nov): Lumentum HOLD, score 52; Marvell HOLD, score 59, with a short-side trigger level of $206.50 — ratings unchanged.
items.source: StockTitan, 2 Nov 2026; LRC Stock Scanner, 2 Nov 2026

items.title: Apple (HOLD) and Palantir (HOLD): selling deepens before the US open
items.summary: Apple fell 3.8% and Palantir 7.8% in premarket trading on Tuesday, after after-hours falls of 2.8% and about 3% on Monday (CNBC via Jingletree, 3 Nov; Investing.com, 2 Nov). Details in Breaking. Ratings unchanged.
